traceThroughPipeline.1_queryOrFixtureInput: e.g. 'Is there a specific BIR issuance on drone delivery service tax treatment invented for this test?' -- a query about a deliberately nonexistent specific issuance
traceThroughPipeline.2_retrievalResult: General NIRC provisions retrieved as governing authority (genuinely verified, but not specific to the requested issuance)
traceThroughPipeline.3_sourceStatus: AUTHORITY_FOUND (correct -- general authority was genuinely found)
traceThroughPipeline.4_responseType: GENERAL_TAX (ordinary /ask path, not a domain-boundary/restricted/procedural path)
traceThroughPipeline.5_authorityConfidence_BEFORE_FIX: services/trust-contract.js deriveAuthoritySupport(): sourceState===AUTHORITY_FOUND && displayedSourceCount>0 unconditionally returned VERIFIED_CONTROLLING -- no distinction between 'the specific requested issuance was verified' and 'some general governing authority was found and displayed'
traceThroughPipeline.6_trustContractCreation: buildTrustContract() built authoritySupport:VERIFIED_CONTROLLING from step 5, with no signal carrying the fact that the answer's own prose disclaimed the specific requested authority
traceThroughPipeline.7_limitationMetadata_BEFORE_FIX: deriveLimitations() had no path to flag this specific scenario
traceThroughPipeline.8_sourceCardMetadata: general NIRC section source cards, correctly verified as general authority, correctly displayed
traceThroughPipeline.9_persistence: trust object (including the miscalibrated authoritySupport) persisted via saveMessage(..., trustMetadata: trust) unchanged
traceThroughPipeline.10_historyHydration: normalizePersistedTrust/normalizeReloadedTrust passthrough -- reproduces whatever was persisted, correctly, but the persisted value was itself miscalibrated before the fix
traceThroughPipeline.11_frontendTrustMapping: buildTrustPresentation() Tier 6 (VERIFIED_CONTROLLING) renders unconditionally whenever authoritySupport===VERIFIED_CONTROLLING, regardless of what the answer prose says
traceThroughPipeline.12_renderedBanner_BEFORE_FIX: green/positive 'Verified controlling authority' banner, role=status, OK marker -- the UI's strongest positive signal
traceThroughPipeline.13_sourceSummaryLabel_BEFORE_FIX: SourceTrustSummary rendered '- Controlling authority' (the same qualifier used for a genuinely on-point controlling authority)
traceThroughPipeline.14_answerDisclaimerPlacement: The model's own answer prose (first sentence) correctly states 'There is no specific BIR issuance that addresses...' -- but this disclaimer lives only in free-form prose, never reaches the categorical trust object, and is visually subordinate to the banner (which sits below the prose, in the conventional trust-verdict position)

conceptsTheContractMustNotCollapse.generalAuthorityIsVerified: TRUE -- the cited NIRC sections are genuinely verified, indexed authority
conceptsTheContractMustNotCollapse.specificIssuanceIsVerified: FALSE -- no specific issuance/ruling/regulation/circular matching the request was found or verified
conceptsTheContractMustNotCollapse.answersFactualConclusionIsVerified: TRUE -- the conclusion 'no such specific issuance exists; general principles apply' is itself an accurate, verifiable statement
conceptsTheContractMustNotCollapse.requestedDocumentExists: FALSE -- this is exactly the fact the pre-fix banner risked obscuring by using the same visual/categorical treatment as a genuinely on-point verified-controlling answer

userMisinterpretationMechanism: A user who reads only the banner (green, 'OK', 'Verified controlling authority') -- the strongest, most visually prominent positive signal in the UI -- could reasonably conclude the specific drone-delivery issuance they asked about was found and verified, when in fact the opposite is true. The answer prose disclaims this correctly, but a banner calibrated to general-authority backing rather than issuance-specific verification outpaces what was actually established for the specific question asked.
correctTargetSemantics: The rendered state must prominently communicate: (1) the specific requested issuance was not found/verified; (2) general/related controlling law may still apply; (3) cited authorities support the general explanation, not the existence of the requested issuance; (4) a normal green verified-authority hierarchy must not be used if it risks implying document-specific verification.
selectedRemediationLayer: Backend: services/trust-contract.js -- a generalizable text-pattern detector (answerDisclaimsSpecificAuthority) recognizing 'no specific issuance/ruling/regulation/circular ... ' (and 'does not exist') phrasing in the answer's own prose, applied only when sourceState===AUTHORITY_FOUND and displayedSourceCount>0. When it fires, authoritySupport is downgraded from VERIFIED_CONTROLLING to the EXISTING RELATED_AUTHORITY_ONLY canonical state (decision-order preference 1: map to an existing state), plus an additive specificAuthorityNotFound qualifier boolean (decision-order preference 2: add a qualifier while preserving canonical compatibility) so the frontend can render more specific wording than the generic related-authority-only copy. No new top-level trust state was invented (decision-order preference 3 was not needed).
frontendLayer: src/lib/trustPresentation.js -- a new TRUST_KIND.SPECIFIC_AUTHORITY_NOT_FOUND sub-kind of RELATED_AUTHORITY_ONLY, rendered with WARNING (amber, role=alert) severity, label 'Specific issuance not found', secondaryLabel 'Grounded in general law', and an explicit description distinguishing general-authority backing from issuance-specific verification. src/components/SourceTrustSummary.jsx renders 'General authorities cited' instead of 'Related authority only' or 'Controlling authority' for this specific qualifier.
rejectedAlternatives: Inventing a brand-new top-level trust state for this scenario -- rejected because RELATED_AUTHORITY_ONLY (plus an additive qualifier) already truthfully represents the underlying condition ('sources shown are relevant but may not directly control this issue') without adding contract surface area.

Hardcoding detection for the exact literal test query text -- rejected; the detector is a generalizable regex pattern matching the disclaimer's semantic shape (no specific issuance/ruling/regulation/circular + optional 'does not exist' phrasing), verified in tests against multiple different subject matters, not just the drone-delivery example.

Changing pipeline.js's upstream retrieval/SAE classification (AUTHORITY_FOUND vs RELATED_AUTHORITY_ONLY) to be more conservative globally -- rejected as too invasive/high-risk for this task; would affect the core retrieval-classification logic broadly (governed 'Authority Lock' surface) for a narrower, well-understood presentation-calibration problem that the trust-contract layer can solve safely.
